2026-09-16: 18.1.21 -> 18.2.1 via `omp update`, verified in-place at D:\OMP\omp.exe (sha256 FEE52652C7B0B90EB7716B3C6DA50AB4D90442505EEF1C5349C9428E8D966679, matching the updater-reported hash); the previous 18.1.21 binary was kept by the updater as omp.exe.1789534362039.11444.0.bak (sha256 61856ACAC3845C3CB8F12C8F6BFB7ECF30E10543AC0EBD69F6FDB404D23C45DA). Binary size 161.7 MB -> 211.7 MB, matching the 18.2.0 change to ship precompiled bytecode. Update requires closing running omp sessions first (Windows cannot replace a locked exe); no duplicate install was created outside D:\OMP and no npm-global omp.cmd shim exists.

RESOLVED 2026-09-16 — root cause found and fixed. The 2026-09-15 claim that OMP reads the user-global rules from %USERPROFILE%\.codex\AGENTS.md was recorded as "verified via omp -p, reproduced the six section headings", but that run happened from inside E:\MachineContext and therefore observed the PROJECT file, not the user-global one. Re-tested properly from a scratch directory containing .git but no AGENTS.md, `omp -p` injected nothing, on 18.2.1 AND on 18.1.21 (controlled A/B swap of the saved .bak) — so it was never a regression from the upgrade. ROOT CAUSE (from the bundled source in omp.exe): the loader is `function Mll(e){ const o = g3(e); if (!o) return {items:[],warnings:[]}; ... }` and `function g3(e, t=false){ if (!t && !dl("codex", e)) return null; return path.join(e.home, d8.codex.userBase); }`. The gate `dl("codex", e)` is a per-provider opt-in check: it fails when the provider is in `disabledProviders`, passes when the provider registry marks it default-on (`X4s[s] !== true`), and otherwise passes only when the provider is in `enabledProviders` (or the registry set contains "*"/"all", or the call passes `explicitProviders`/`includeOptOutUserSources`). `codex` is a default-off (opt-in) context-source provider, and `omp config get enabledProviders` returned `[]`, so `g3` returned null and the whole Codex user-global source short-circuited — silently, with no warning. FIX APPLIED: `omp config set enabledProviders '["codex"]'` (note the JSON-array argument form; a bare `codex` is rejected with "Invalid array JSON"). That persists a top-level `enabledProviders: [codex]` to %USERPROFILE%\.omp\agent\config.yml (1046 -> 1074 bytes; pre-change copy saved at .local/backup-omp-config-2026-09-16.yml). VERIFIED after the fix with no overlay: from a scratch project with only .git, `omp -p` reports COUNT=6 LANG=chinese, i.e. the shared global ruleset (6 Chinese headings) — previously NONE. CORRECTED (2026-09-16, later the same session): an earlier version of this note claimed OMP surfaces the project-level AGENTS.md *instead of* the user-global one. That was WRONG and is retracted here. The claim came from a COUNT=6/LANG= test whose answer was careless; the verbatim-heading probe shows OMP loads BOTH additively - from E:\MachineContext the visible headings are the 6 Chinese ones (global) AND the 6 English ones (project), while from a scratch directory with no AGENTS.md only the 6 Chinese ones appear. So OMP has the same semantics as Codex here: user-global personal rules plus project rules, both in context. METHOD LESSON: do not decide this class of question from a model's own count/summary; require verbatim enumeration, because a summary answer can be wrong in a way that looks like a clean A/B result. Enabling the `codex` provider also turns on the other Codex-compat sources (~/.codex/skills, extensions, commands, prompts, hooks, tools); those directories do not exist here (only the global AGENTS.md is present), so this had no other effect. NOTE: `provider` here means a context-source provider id, not an LLM provider - and such a provider being default-off means it must be opted into via enabledProviders, which is not the same as an opt-out provider.
